hypotheses.text: Congenital anterior pituitary hypoplasia or aplasia is present in over 80% of individuals with biallelic TBC1D32-associated Alsahan-Harris syndrome, serving as the primary neuroimaging feature that distinguishes ALHAS from classic Joubert syndrome and classic Orofaciodigital syndrome IX.
hypotheses.rationale: While many ciliopathies cause midline brain malformations and polydactyly, severe developmental failure of the adenohypophysis (ranging from mild hypoplasia to complete absence) is reported repeatedly across unrelated pediatric and fetal TBC1D32 cohorts, making it the most discriminating positive neuroimaging sign.

evidence.text: Harris et al. identified an affected individual diagnosed with an absent pituitary gland on fetal autopsy, noting that an absent pituitary gland was also documented in four pediatric patients out of seven previously published or cohort cases.

source.title: Diagnosis of TBC1D32‐associated conditions: Expanding the phenotypic spectrum of a complex ciliopathy
source.quote: We also present an affected individual diagnosed with an absent pituitary gland by fetal autopsy, a finding reported in four of the pediatric patients.

evidence.text: Biallelic loss-of-function variants in TBC1D32 in two Finnish siblings caused panhypopituitarism with absent anterior pituitary, while a Pakistani proband with a homozygous splice variant had anterior pituitary hypoplasia and growth hormone deficiency.

hypotheses.text: Retinal dystrophy/retinopathy is a hallmark manifestation present in >75% of post-neonatal survivors with Alsahan-Harris syndrome, but is absent or unassessable in lethal fetal presentations.
hypotheses.rationale: Testing whether retinal dystrophy consistently emerges postnatally differentiates viable pediatric TBC1D32 ciliopathy cases from other orofaciodigital syndromes lacking retinal degeneration, and helps clinicians establish age-dependent screening criteria.

evidence.text: A literature review and case series of two unrelated patients identified facial dysmorphism, retinal disease, and hypopituitarism as the three cardinal clinical features defining TBC1D32-related ciliopathy in viable patients.

source.title: Expanding the clinical and molecular spectrum of TBC1D32-related ciliopathy: case reports and literature Review
source.quote: A review of previously reported cases highlighted facial dysmorphism, retinal disease, and hypopituitarism as major clinical features of TBC1D32-related ciliopathy.

numbers.metric: new probands with retinal disease and hypopituitarism

hypotheses.text: Oculomotor nerve palsy is a specific cranial nerve manifestation of TBC1D32 disruption reflecting midbrain/hindbrain developmental pathology, which reliably distinguishes Alsahan-Harris syndrome from Pallister-Hall syndrome.
hypotheses.rationale: Pallister-Hall syndrome and Alsahan-Harris syndrome both display hypothalamic-pituitary disruption and postaxial/mesoaxial polydactyly, but cranial neuropathies such as oculomotor palsy occur in ciliary hindbrain dysgenesis and have not been described in Pallister-Hall syndrome.

evidence.text: In a 2025 clinical evaluation of two unrelated patients with biallelic TBC1D32 splice-site variants leading to exon skipping, unilateral oculomotor nerve palsy was observed and proposed as an extended clinical feature of this ciliopathy.

source.title: Expanding the clinical and molecular spectrum of TBC1D32-related ciliopathy: case reports and literature Review
source.quote: We report two unrelated patients with retinal disease and hypopituitarism, with one also exhibiting facial dysmorphism, developmental delay, and unilateral oculomotor nerve palsy... Additionally, we propose oculomotor nerve palsy as an extended clinical feature of this disorder.

new_directions.question_text: What is the systematic frequency of specific craniofacial features (e.g., long philtrum, microcephaly, brachycephaly, cleft lip) across all published TBC1D32 cohorts, and how do they discriminate ALHAS from isolated growth hormone deficiency?
new_directions.rationale: Multiple sources describe characteristic facial dysmorphisms alongside pituitary hypoplasia. Quantifying exact numerator/denominator frequencies will establish whether dysmorphic exam findings can definitively separate ALHAS from idiopathic or isolated genetic hypopituitarism.

new_directions.question_text: Does the presence of structural hindbrain malformations (e.g., molar tooth sign) correlate with the severity of TBC1D32 variant type (biallelic null vs. hypomorphic splice-site/missense)?
new_directions.rationale: Clarifying whether classic Joubert-like hindbrain signs occur predominantly with severe loss-of-function variants will refine genotype-phenotype correlations between OFD-IX, classic Joubert, and prenatal-lethal ALHAS.
